P1: Dark card. Taiwan trial court, rental deposit. Headline: Never signed the lease. Still lost the deposit case. Drawing of an unsigned lease and a slip reading Deposit wired NT$21,800. The court said the lease was formed at the viewing; the renter backed out the same day.
Made-up scene, renter's side. Boxes in an empty room under the renter's speech bubble: My stuff won't fit. I'm out. Nothing was signed, so they wanted the money back. The company said no.
Made-up scene, company's side. Speech bubble: Rent's set. The ad said 1 year. A note shows NT$21,800 a month and a one-year minimum, and the company says it canceled 3 other viewings.
Message quoted in the ruling, translated from Chinese: the renter's LINE message after wiring the money, sent as the rental deposit. The renter gave this chat to the court.

The ruling: no refund owed. An unsigned lease beside the terms agreed at the viewing (NT$21,800 a month, one-year minimum) and the LINE wording 承租訂金. The lease existed from the viewing day, and backing out over space was on the renter.

Taiwan Civil Code Art. 249, default rule. If the payer's fault means the contract can't be carried out, zero comes back. If it's the recipient's fault, double is paid back. That applies if the parties agreed nothing else; if neither side is at fault, the money is returned.
P2: Dark card. Taiwan trial court, divorce by agreement. Headline: Divorce registered. Court says: still married. A divorce agreement marked Registered with a VOID stamp. One witness never asked the husband if he really wanted out.
Made-up scene based on testimony. A divorce agreement on a restaurant table with the couple's lines blank. The wife asks a friend: Can you sign as a witness here? Only the two of them were there.

Paraphrased testimony. The friend in court: I don't have her husband's number. Never met the husband before or after signing, never asked him about a divorce, didn't go on registration day. Neither spouse disputed it, and the court didn't count the friend as a witness.

Diagram of witness rules: husband, wife, the friend, and the other witness. The friend never checked with the husband and talked only to the wife; the other witness was not ruled on. A witness must see or hear that both spouses want out; secondhand doesn't count.

Taiwan divorce by agreement, three requirements: in writing (met), 2+ qualified witnesses sign (not met here), registered at the office (met). Even counting the other witness, fewer than two, so void. Each witness must see or hear that both spouses want out (case law).
P3: Dark card. Taiwan court, bus ran a red light. Headline: Kid's dental claim: all awarded. Parent's lost income: under a tenth. Two bars comparing claimed and awarded amounts: future dental costs all awarded, lost income under a tenth. The parent filed no income records.
Made-up scene. Top view of an intersection with a red light and a scooter hitting the side of a bus. The parent says: The bus just ran the red light. Taipei, 2020, with the kid on the back.
Injuries in the ruling. Four upper front teeth: 1 knocked out, 3 broken. The parent: broken left collarbone.

The ruling: future dental costs, full claim, NT$343,000, based on the implant plan, which leaves the method open until adulthood. The court's reason: the kid was still a minor, and teeth affect how a face looks. The driver and bus company pushed a cheaper NT$120k–150k option.

Parent's claim: income lost while recovering went from NT$385,022 to NT$27,808, the amount the defense itself put forward. The defense said a part-timer covered the breakfast shop: NT$158 an hour × 8 hours × 22 days.

Worth knowing. Injury: the doctor's note. Lost income: pay records. The doctor's note (rest 4 weeks after surgery) shows the time you had to rest; filed here. Pay slips and tax returns show the money you lost; not filed here. With no income records filed, the court used the 4-week note and the defense's figure.
